subject: Commercial clarification: bucketed commits, true-up cadence, and token mapping
messages:
From: Linda Zhao <linda.zhao@finservcorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, procurement@finservcorp.com
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP: Commercial questions on commits and overage handling

Ben — thanks for the walkthrough last week. The evaluation committee asked for a concise commercial summary we can include in the RFP response. Specific items they flagged: 1) how committed token buckets are defined (calendar month vs. rolling 30d), 2) how embeddings are priced/converted vs. generations, 3) true-up cadence and invoicing (monthly/quarterly), and 4) your approach to discounts over multi-year commits and early termination credits.

Can you provide a short, clear answer for each point plus any example math for a hypothetical 100M token/year commit with a 30% embed mix? Also please attach the commercial appendix you referenced.

Thanks,
Linda Zhao
Director, Sourcing — FinServ Corporation

Attachment: RFP-Sections-FinServ-v3.docx (docx)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Linda Zhao <linda.zhao@finservcorp.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-02T14:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Commercial questions on commits and overage handling

Linda — appreciate the clear list. See answers below and attached commercial appendix + an illustrative worksheet. Quick TL;DR first: we price on committed token units (calendar month buckets by default), embed tokens are charged at a 0.6x factor relative to generation tokens for billing, true-ups are quarterly by default with monthly reporting, and multi-year discounts follow a step-down schedule tied to the committed annual volume with pro-rated early termination credits for remaining committed value (see examples).

Detailed answers: 1) Commit buckets: we bill against calendar-month buckets (e.g., Nov 1–30). Customers can opt-in to a rolling-30 policy for workloads with irregular seasonality; that requires a 5% admin surcharge due to accounting complexity. Commits are denominated in tokens (not requests).

2) Embedding vs generation mapping: embeddings consume smaller per-request tokens but to simplify procurement we provide a convertible mapping: 1 embedding = 0.6 generation tokens for commercial reconciliation. For example, 100M tokens/year commit with 30% embedding mix is treated as 100M * (0.7 + 0.6*0.3) = 91M effective generation tokens for pricing and true-up.

3) True-up cadence & invoicing: monthly usage reporting (detailed token breakdown) with quarterly invoicing/true-up by default. We issue an invoice for committed minimums at month-end and reconcile over/under usage at quarter close — net overages billed on the quarterly invoice. Customers can elect monthly true-up for a 1% processing fee.

4) Multi-year discounts & early termination: discounts are applied as % off list token price tied to annual committed bands (see attached worksheet). Example: 1-year 100M commit = 8% discount; 2-year same annual commit = 12% year-1, 14% year-2 price by dollar-weighted model. If customer terminates early we credit remaining committed dollars as an amortized credit spread across remaining months (subject to minimum notice and a 3% administrative fee).

Attached: Redwood-Commit-Pricing-Worksheet.xlsx (xlsx); RFP-Commercial-Appendix-FS-v3.pdf (pdf)

Happy to convert any of this into a single-page commercial summary for the committee.

— Ben Carter
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — couple of follow-ups from the procurement review board: 1) your example math for embedding conversion (0.6x) is reasonable, can you confirm whether the factor is fixed or model-dependent? 2) we need clarity on rollover behavior: if a customer under-uses in Q1 and over-uses in Q2, do unused tokens roll forward across quarters? 3) for committed pools with dedicated capacity (Dedicated plan), how do you compute effective utilization and idle-credit rules?

Linda — copying because these are material commercial clarifications.

— Andy

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Andy Park <andy.park@ogdenpartners.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Linda Zhao <linda.zhao@finservcorp.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-06T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Commercial questions on commits and overage handling

Andy/Linda — answers inline: 1) Embedding factor: default 0.6x is our standard commercial conversion for the models we typically recommend. It is model-group dependent in engineering (some retriever-focused embedding models are ~0.55x), but for contracting we treat 0.6x as the standard; we can include a model-specific appendix if you require absolute billing parity. 2) Rollover behavior: unused committed units do not automatically roll forward across quarters under standard terms because commits are annual/banded with quarterly true-up; however, customers may elect a 1-quarter rollover for up to 10% of their quarterly commit if they provide 30 days notice before the quarter end. Rollover beyond one quarter is escalated to finance and usually requires a minimum annual commit increase. 3) Dedicated capacity: for Dedicated customers we track "effective utilization" as (billed tokens consumed / theoretical max tokens deliverable by provisioned GPUs over the same period). Idle-credit rules: if average utilization falls below 40% for two consecutive months, customers can request a proportional credit up to 20% of that month's committed charge (requires review). Credits are capped annually to avoid double-counting with autoscale/burst credits.

If you want, Markus and Karthik can provide the worked examples for your specific 100M/year scenario and show how Dedicated capacity amortizes.

— Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Andy Park <andy.park@ogdenpartners.com>, Linda Zhao <linda.zhao@finservcorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-10T11:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Commercial questions on commits and overage handling

Andy/Linda — attached is the detailed worksheet and two scenarios for the 100M token/year example (shared as XLSX): Scenario A: Hosted (no dedicated GPUs) with 30% embeddings; Scenario B: Dedicated pool sized for peak with assumed 60% average utilization. Key numbers summarized: 
- Scenario A: effective billing tokens = 91M (per Ben's formula); list unit price $0.000015/token; net price after 8% commit discount = $0.0000138/token; annual cost ≈ $1,255,800. Quarterly true-up applies.
- Scenario B: assumes dedicated infra fee of $75k/month + unit price discounted to $0.000010/token (volume + dedicated commitment), effective annual cost ≈ $1,095,000 at 60% utilization. If utilization dips <40% for two months we trigger idle-credit review.

Rollover example: Q1 under-use = 2M tokens; Q2 over-use = 3M tokens => with 1-quarter rollover elected, 2M carries forward, net Q2 overage = 1M. Without rollover, full 3M overage billed at contracted overage rate.

I've also included the draft contract clause text we typically include for true-ups and early termination (see attachment DocuSign-FS-Statement-of-Work-draft.pdf). Happy to walk through the spreadsheet in a short call.

— Markus Klein
Director, Pricing & Go-to-Market Finance
Redwood Inference
